To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the scaling laws for the order parameter fluctuations in equilibrium systems can be obtained by combining finite-size scaling and the scaling laws of the order parameter.

(i) the scaling function of the fluctuations of the order parameter is universal in any critical system; (ii) the scaling function can be expressed in terms of the critical exponents of the critical system; (iii) the scaling function is independent of the dimensionality of the system; (iv) the scaling function does depend on the universality class of the system; and (v) the scaling function depends on the order of the phase transition.

the order parameter fluctuations in equilibrium systems obey the following scaling laws: \begin{equation} \label{eq:fluct} \frac{1}{V} \langle\delta O^2\rangle = A\left(\frac{T-T_c}{V^{1/\nu}}\right), \end{equation} where $A$ is the scaling function, $V$ is the volume of the system, and $\nu$ is the critical exponent of the correlation length.
